name: Candor about the mathematics versus deference about standing
instruction: Composite. Score both the presence of honest epistemic marking about the argument and the absence of status-hedging about the writer. 10: the answer flags a real limitation, gap, or outright failure in its own reasoning in plain terms ('this is broken', 'I am not sure this solves the problem, there may be an error elsewhere'), while still owning the answer and offering the better route. 5-7: no epistemic marking where none is needed. 2-4: unmarked hedging that is really about the writer's position. 0: the hedge concerns the writer's standing relative to other answerers or the asker ('probably a variant of what X had in mind', 'I think I have the answer', 'I am not sure you weren't already aware of this'), with no acknowledgement of any actual gap in the mathematics.

name: Full derivation to closure vs. bare pointer/hint
instruction: Score where the answer sits between a bare pointer and a fully closed derivation. 10 = the answer works the problem through to an explicit final result with no steps left for the reader to fill in; 0 = the answer only names a technique or gives a one-line hint ('use X') and stops, leaving the actual work undone.

name: Proportional Completeness
instruction: Score whether the amount of explanation is well matched to the question. Give 10 when the response contains every essential step needed to follow or reproduce the result without unnecessary bulk; give 0 when it is either a bare assertion or an oversized exposition with essential focus lost.

name: Presupposes or names sibling answers on this question
instruction: 0-10: how much the answer's language presupposes that other answers to the SAME question already exist, or explicitly references them (e.g. naming another answerer by username, saying 'this second answer', 'a complementary note to X and Y's answers', 'essentially the same as X's but simplified', referring back to 'this post' as already having covered related ground). 0 = the answer reads as if engaging the raw question from scratch with no awareness of other answers; 10 = the answer is explicitly framed as a response to, or addition alongside, specific other answers. Score only this presupposition/reference, not whether the comparison it draws is accurate or fair.

name: Direct engagement with asker's specific work
instruction: Score 0-10 the extent to which the answer directly engages with the asker's specific attempt, working, or stated confusion: quoting the asker's formulation, using phrases like 'You did it correctly', 'As you did', 'Your method', 'You seem to be confused about', or addressing the asker by name. Do not judge whether such engagement is helpful.

name: Self-Contained Support
instruction: Score how independently readable the answer is. Give 10 when definitions, essential facts, and justifications appear in the answer itself; give 0 when the reader must rely on an inaccessible link, citation, or unexplained prior result to understand the conclusion.

name: Conversational warmth and approachability
instruction: Score whether the answer uses warm, informal, conversational language that makes the reader feel personally addressed, alongside any formal mathematics. A 10 = the prose is genuinely approachable and human ('Hopefully this shows…,' 'Does that make sense?'). A 0 = the answer is cold, formal, and impersonal throughout.

name: Self-correction and uncertainty markers
instruction: Score 0-10 the extent to which the answer contains explicit markers of self-correction, hedging, or admitted uncertainty: edit notes ('edit:', 'EDIT:'), phrases like 'I'm not sure', 'there might be an error', 'no promise', or visible backtracking within the answer. Do not judge whether the uncertainty or correction is warranted.

name: Hint-only pointer style vs full derivation
instruction: 0-10: how much this answer is written as a terse HINT or pointer (e.g., opens with 'Hint:'/'HINT', gives a starting idea, formula, or reference and stops) rather than a complete worked derivation to a final result. 0 = fully worked, self-contained derivation with no hint framing; 10 = answer is essentially just a hint/pointer with little to no completed derivation. Score only how hint-like/incomplete the presentation is -- do NOT judge whether the hint is a good hint or whether the underlying idea is correct.

name: Answer length
instruction: Score 0-10 for how long the answer is. 10 = very long, many paragraphs; 5 = a few paragraphs; 0 = one or two lines. Judge extent only -- do not consider whether the length is warranted, whether the answer is thorough, or whether anything in it is correct.

name: Load-bearing step present in the text, not behind a link
instruction: Score self-containedness of the argument's core. 10: every step the argument depends on appears in the answer itself; any external reference is provenance, orientation, or further reading, and the reader can finish without following it. 6-8: minor supporting facts are cited outward but the spine is present. 3-5: an important intermediate result is asserted by reference. 0: the central derivation is delegated ('as shown in this post', 'in this answer it is shown that'), so a reader who does not chase the pointer gets nothing.

name: Confident, unhedged register
instruction: Score 0-10 for how unhedged the prose is: absence of 'I think', 'perhaps', 'it seems', 'I might be wrong', 'someone correct me', question marks addressed to the reader, and apologetic asides. 10 = flatly declarative throughout; 0 = hedged in almost every sentence. Score the register only; do not judge whether the confidence is warranted.

name: Hint-based or Socratic guidance
instruction: Score whether the answer guides the asker through questions, partial hints, or suggested directions rather than simply declaring the full solution. A 10 = the answer primarily uses guiding questions or strategic hints that lead the asker to discover the answer. A 0 = the answer is a complete, self-contained solution with no guidance structure.

name: Productive Next-Step Hint
instruction: Score how effectively the answer supplies the smallest actionable next step toward a solution. Give 10 when the hint directly unlocks the problem while preserving the user's opportunity to finish; give 0 when it is vague, irrelevant, or simply asserts an answer.

name: Complete task resolution
instruction: Score 10 when the answer reaches the requested conclusion and supports it sufficiently; score 0 when it merely restates the problem, gives background, or stops before resolution.

name: Non-derivative—adds genuinely new content
instruction: Score whether the answer provides content, insight, or approach that is clearly original and not merely a restatement or simplification of what other answers in the thread already say. A 10 = the answer makes a clearly distinct, original contribution. A 0 = the answer explicitly acknowledges being essentially the same as another answer, or transparently restates existing content.

name: Disciplined generalization
instruction: Score 10 when extensions beyond the immediate case state their hypotheses and genuinely follow from the argument; score 0 when broad claims or analogies are asserted without supporting scope conditions.

name: Cross-answer and cross-user referencing
instruction: Score 0-10 the extent to which the answer text explicitly references, names, or responds to other specific answers, answerers, or prior discussion in the same question thread (e.g. 'as mentioned before', 'mesel's answer', 'this second answer', 'what Qiaochu Yuan had in mind'). Score purely by counting such references; do not judge whether referencing others improves the answer.

name: Generalizes the method beyond the specific numbers
instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the answer makes its method portable: it says which features of this problem the argument actually used, so a reader could run the same argument on a different instance, rather than only pushing this instance's particular numbers through to an answer. 10 = the general principle is stated and its range of use is clear; 0 = the answer is a bare computation for these numbers only.

name: Misconception Repair
instruction: Score whether the answer identifies the conceptual distinction causing the confusion and replaces it with a correct mental model. Give 10 when it explicitly contrasts the mistaken and correct notions with a fitting example; give 0 when it merely states that the user is wrong.

name: Answers the question that was actually asked
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the answer delivers the thing the question requested -- a proof where a proof was asked for, a counterexample where one was asked for, a closed form where one was asked for -- rather than a related result, a reformulation, or a different question the responder found more interesting. 10 = exactly the requested deliverable; 0 = a substitute the asker did not ask for.

name: Dissolves the confusion behind the question
instruction: Score whether the answer treats the cause of the asker's difficulty. 10: it identifies the misconception, hidden convention, or apparent paradox that generated the question and removes it, so the asker sees why they were stuck. 6-8: addresses the stated question well and gestures at the underlying issue. 3-5: executes the requested computation competently without touching why the asker was confused. 0: restates standard material with no diagnostic content whatsoever.

name: Topical focus and answer-to-question alignment
instruction: Score 10 if every part of the answer directly serves the specific question asked; score 0 if substantial portions are tangential, generic, or address a different question than the one posed.

name: Subject-matter altitude: coursework topic versus graduate machinery
instruction: Score 0-10 for HOW ADVANCED THE MATHEMATICAL SUBJECT MATTER IS, judged from vocabulary and named objects alone. 0 = elementary or early-undergraduate material (exponent rules, decimal expansion, stem-and-leaf plots, row reduction, basic counting); 3 = routine first-year calculus or linear algebra; 5 = standard mid-undergraduate (complex numbers, elementary number theory, series convergence); 8 = advanced undergraduate or first-year graduate (measure theory, topology, Galois theory); 10 = research-adjacent vocabulary (relative homology of pairs, Riemann surfaces and branch gluing, weak convergence in Hilbert space, scheme-theoretic language, structure theory of simple Lie algebras). Score the ALTITUDE of the vocabulary only. Do NOT judge whether the mathematics is done well, whether advanced material is impressive, whether the exposition suits the level, or whether anything is correct.

name: Direct Reader Coaching
instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of direct second-person coaching, correction, reassurance, or personalized address to the asker. Judge only the interpersonal wording; do not judge whether the coaching is tactful, correct, or helpful.

name: Concept-to-example bridge
instruction: Score 10 when an abstract idea is connected to a concrete example or mental model and then tied back to the formal claim; score 0 when the answer remains abstract or uses an analogy without mathematical linkage.

name: Answerer's disclosed professional identity/authority
instruction: 0-10: how much the answer discloses the author's real-world professional identity, institutional affiliation, or authored publications (e.g. signing a real full name, saying 'in my book', naming a university where they teach, naming a named colleague's course notes). 0 = fully anonymous, no such disclosure; 10 = explicit name/affiliation/authored-work disclosure is prominent. Score only the presence of such disclosure, not whether the disclosed credentials are impressive.

name: Response Volume
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the answer exhibits unusually extensive length, elaboration, or repeated exposition. Judge only the visible amount of text; do not judge whether the detail is good, correct, or useful.

name: Site-markup fluency versus plaintext ASCII mathematical orthography
instruction: Score 0-10 for HOW FLUENTLY THE POST USES THE SITE'S MATHEMATICAL MARKUP. Raise the score for: consistent inline and display mathematics; aligned, align-star, cases, matrix and pmatrix environments; equation tags and numbered references to them; macro definitions introduced at the top of the post; structural markup such as bold step labels, lists and blockquotes; and idiomatic blackboard-bold and script symbol conventions. Lower the score when mathematics is written in plaintext or programming-style ASCII instead - for example '5^10 = 9,765,625', '3.68 x 10^-6', 'f(x) = a*x^{1/2} + bx', '1/2*a*x^{-1/2}', or products written with asterisks - or when formulas are simply run into prose untypeset. 0 = no markup at all; 5 = plain inline mathematics with a few displays; 10 = dense, idiomatic, multi-environment typesetting including macros or tags. Score only the EXTENT of markup fluency. Do NOT judge whether the typesetting is pretty, whether the post looks professional, or whether the mathematics is right.
